source.title: Higher Siegel–Weil formula for unitary groups: the non-singular terms
source.authors: Tony Feng, Zhiwei Yun and Wei Zhang
readSections: The whole published article (§§1–12 and the references), open access under CC BY 4.0 from link.springer.com, 100 pp., SHA-256 f4ebe96fe481209f41421b0bb0b2c9d27313e5d39f6e0065972c2e90a3155fcd, fetched and read 2026-09-22. Locators are its journal pages.

arXiv 2103.11514v4 (29 November 2023), 79 pp., SHA-256 c6a65b8c01333cc726ba6b163fd24aba5022db6cf5baf00c353ccb9b9ba182b8: the two versions carry exactly the same 112 numbered statements, and each recorded misprint was checked to read the same there.

summary:
Feng, Yun and Zhang prove a function-field analogue of the Kudla–Rapoport conjecture that computes every Taylor coefficient, not only the first, of a non-singular Fourier coefficient of a Siegel–Eisenstein series. For an étale double cover ν : X′ → X of curves over F_q (q odd), a rank n bundle E on X′ and an injective Hermitian map a : E → σ^*E^∨, Theorem 1.1 reads (1/(log q)^r)(d/ds)^r|_{s=0}(q^{ds}Ẽ_a(m(E), s, Φ)) = deg[Z^r_E(a)], where Z^r_E(a) is a special cycle on the moduli Sht^r_{U(n)} of Hermitian shtukas with r legs. For r = 0 it is the classical Siegel–Weil formula; for r = 1 it is the analogue of the arithmetic Siegel–Weil formula; and it is the first higher-derivative formula for groups of arbitrary rank.

The proof realizes both sides through the sheaf-to-function dictionary from graded perverse sheaves on the moduli stack Herm_{2d}(X′/X) of Hermitian torsion sheaves.
- **Analytic side (§§2–5).** The non-singular coefficients are local Siegel series (Theorem 2.8), for which the Cho–Yamauchi formula — extended here to the split case (Theorem 2.3) — depends only on the Hermitian torsion sheaf coker(a). A Hermitian Springer theory on Herm_{2d}(X′/X), with Weyl group W_d = (Z/2)^d ⋊ S_d and the local model [o_{2d}/O_{2d}], geometrizes it: Den(T, Q) = Tr(Fr, K^{Eis}_d(T)_Q) (Theorem 5.3).
- **Geometric side (§§6–11).** Special cycles Z^r_E(a) on Sht^r_{U(n)} are constructed after Kudla–Rapoport; they have larger than expected dimension, so a virtual class is built from corank-one cycles and good framings, and shown to be intrinsic by redoing the intersections in a different order through Hitchin-type moduli stacks M(n, n) (Theorem 10.1). The Hitchin fibration is small over Herm_{2d} through Lagr_{2d}, and the Lefschetz trace formula for Hitchin shtukas turns deg[Z^r_E(a)] into Σ_i(d−2i)^rTr(Fr, Spr^{Herm}_{2d}[ρ_i]_Q) (Corollary 11.9).
- **Comparison (§12).** The two sheaves agree, K^{Int}_d ≅ K^{Eis}_d, because of an identity of graded virtual W_d-representations (Lemma 12.4).

The libraries have none of this. The atlas plans the surrounding machinery — shtuka stacks (GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands GS.0–GS.2), perverse sheaves and the decomposition theorem (EDC.5, EDC.7), cohomological correspondences and the trace formula (EDC.8, R34.1), Chow groups with refined Gysin maps (SF.5), local densities (GN.3) and automorphic forms over function fields (FA.6) — but no cycles on shtuka moduli, no Hitchin fibration outside Ngô's setting, and no global Springer theory.

Routes: a new Part II ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil of GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands for the cycles, the Springer theory, the Hitchin stacks and the formula; sources for GN.3 (the Hermitian local densities and the Cho–Yamauchi formula in both inert and split cases) and FA.6 (the Siegel–Eisenstein series over a function field and its Fourier coefficients).

Three misprints are recorded; no mathematical error or gap was found. The two key representation-theoretic inputs, Lemma 12.4 and the decomposition (11.5) with the irreducibility of its summands, were verified by character computation for d ≤ 4. The independent review confirmed E1–E3 and added E4–E28. The most substantive is E22: Lemma 10.5's claim that u_1 is étale fails for some very good framings, and its proof uses a false isomorphism, but the maps w_1 and h_1 actually used are étale by a corrected argument. Among the others: two proof gaps in §§6–7 (Lemma 6.7 for X_{k′}, Lemma 7.6 over imperfect fields); a misprinted weight in Remark 2.4; and an overstatement at the start of §9. None affects Theorem 1.1. The review also split off item 34 (the U(n)-specific Lemmas 6.7 and 6.9) and corrected the modification convention in item 15.

items.name: Theorem 1.1 (the higher Siegel–Weil formula for non-singular Fourier coefficients)
items.statement: Let X be a smooth proper geometrically connected curve over k = F_q (char ≠ 2), ν : X′ → X an étale double cover with involution σ (X′ = X ⊔ X allowed), n ≥ 1 and r ≥ 0. Let E be a rank n vector bundle on X′ and a : E → σ^*E^∨ an injective Hermitian map (E^∨ = Hom(E, ω_{X′})). Then (1/(log q)^r)(d/ds)^r|_{s=0}(q^{ds}·Ẽ_a(m(E), s, Φ)) = deg[Z^r_E(a)], where d = −deg(E) + n deg ω_X = −χ(X′, E), Ẽ_a(m(E), s, Φ) = E_a(m(E), s, Φ)·χ(det E)^{−1}q^{deg(E)(s−n/2)+n²deg(ω_X)/2}·L_n(s) = Den(q^{−2s}, (E, a)) (12.1) is the normalized a-th Fourier coefficient of the Siegel–Eisenstein series of the standard split F′/F-skew-Hermitian space of dimension 2n, and [Z^r_E(a)] ∈ Ch_0(Z^r_E(a)) is the virtual fundamental class of the special cycle on the moduli of Hermitian shtukas with r legs.
items.locator: Theorem 1.1, p. 572; restated and proved as Theorem 12.1, p. 662, published version
items.note: The identity holds for every r, whatever the vanishing order of the Eisenstein coefficient: it unites the Siegel–Weil formula (r = 0, Remark 1.2) and the arithmetic Siegel–Weil formula (the Kudla–Rapoport conjecture over number fields) in one statement, and is the first higher-derivative formula for groups of arbitrary rank. Routed to the new Part II ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil (parent GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands). For odd r both sides of Theorem 1.1 vanish under the paper's hypotheses (Remark 1.2).

items.name: §1.2 (the strategy: two graded perverse sheaves on Herm_{2d}(X′/X) and their matching)
items.statement: Both sides of Theorem 1.1 are realized by the sheaf-to-function dictionary from graded (virtual) perverse sheaves on the moduli stack Herm_{2d}(X′/X) of Hermitian torsion sheaves of length 2d: (1) K^{Eis}_d = ⊕_{i=0}^d K^{Eis}_{d,i} with Ẽ_a(m(E), s, Φ) = Σ_i Tr(Fr_Q, (K^{Eis}_{d,i})_Q)q^{−2is}; (2) K^{Int}_d = ⊕_i K^{Int}_{d,i} with deg[Z^r_E(a)] = Σ_i Tr(Fr_Q, (K^{Int}_{d,i})_Q)(d − 2i)^r; (3) K^{Eis}_d ≅ K^{Int}_d. Both are built from isotypic summands of a Hermitian Springer sheaf under the Weyl group W_d = (Z/2Z)^d ⋊ S_d, so the theorem reduces to an identity of graded virtual W_d-representations.
items.note: Routed to the new Part II ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil (parent GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands).

items.name: §2.1–2.2 (Siegel–Eisenstein series on the quasi-split unitary group over a function field and its Fourier expansion)
items.statement: W is the standard split F′/F-skew-Hermitian space of dimension 2n, H_n = U(W) with Siegel parabolic P_n = M_nN_n, m(α) and n(β) as usual; η is the quadratic idele class character of F′/F and χ a character of A^×_{F′}/F′^× with χ|_{A^×_F} = η^n, which can be chosen everywhere unramified (Remark 2.1). With the unramified standard section Φ normalized by Φ(1_{2n}, s) = 1 in the degenerate principal series I_n(s, χ) = Ind^{H_n(A)}_{P_n(A)}(χ·|·|^{s+n/2}_{F′}), E(g, s, Φ) = Σ_{P_n(F)\H_n(F)}Φ(γg, s) converges for ℜ(s) ≫ 0 and continues meromorphically; its Fourier expansion along N_n is indexed by Hermitian matrices, and the coefficients at m(E) are indexed by Hermitian maps a : E → σ^*E^∨ for a vector bundle E of rank n on X′.
items.note: Routed to FunctionFieldArithmetic FA.6 as a source.

items.name: §2.3–2.4 (local representation densities and the normalized local Siegel series Den(T, L))
items.statement: For Hermitian O_{F′}-lattices M, L the representation density Den(M, L) is the limit of the normalized counts of representations mod ϖ^N; m(a; T) := Π_{i=0}^{a−1}(1 − (η(ϖ)q)^iT); for a torsion O_F-module T, ℓ(T) is its length and t(T) = dim_k(T ⊗ k), with ℓ′, t′ the O_{F′}-versions in the inert case and ℓ = 2ℓ′, t = 2t′; the type of a Hermitian lattice is t(L) = t(L^∨/L). In the split case F′ = F × F a Hermitian lattice is a pair L = (L_1, L_2), and ℓ′ and t′ are defined through the pair, with t′(L) := t′(L^∨/L); the paper's notation for the split dual is used inconsistently between pp. 10 and 11 (E6).
items.note: Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.3 as a source.

items.name: Theorem 2.3 and Remarks 2.4–2.6 (the Cho–Yamauchi formula for Hermitian local densities, including the split case)
items.statement: Let F′/F be unramified or split. For the self-dual Hermitian lattice ⟨1⟩_j of rank j: (1) Den(⟨1⟩_{n+j}, ⟨1⟩_n) = Π_{i=1}^n(1 − (η(ϖ)q)^{−i}T)|_{T=(η(ϖ)q)^{−j}}. (2) There is a unique polynomial Den(T, L) ∈ Z[T] with Den((η(ϖ)q)^{−j}, L) = Den(⟨1⟩_{n+j}, L)/Den(⟨1⟩_{n+j}, ⟨1⟩_n) for all j ≥ 0. (3) Den(T, L) = Σ_{L ⊆ L′ ⊆ (L′)^∨ ⊆ L^∨}T^{2ℓ′(L′/L)}m(t′(L′); T). Consequently Den(T, L) depends only on the Hermitian torsion module L^∨/L, so one may write Den(T, Q) = Σ_{Q′ ⊂ Q′^⊥ ⊂ Q}T^{2ℓ′(Q′)}m(t′(Q′^⊥/Q′); T) for a Hermitian torsion module Q (Remark 2.4; the paper prints m(t′(Q′); T), E4); Remark 2.5 gives the split form of the sum, and Remark 2.6 the functional equation Den(T, L) = (η(ϖ)T)^{ℓ′(L^∨/L)}Den(1/T, L), whence deg Den(T, L) = ℓ′(L^∨/L).
items.locator: Theorem 2.3 and Remarks 2.4–2.6, pp. 581–583, published version
items.note: This is the unitary Cho–Yamauchi formula of [3] as developed in Li–Zhang [18], extended here to the split case. Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.3 as a source. The paper cites a proof of the functional equation (Remark 2.6) only in the inert case ([Hir12]); the split case was checked numerically for n ≤ 2 by the review.

items.name: Lemma 2.7 and Theorem 2.8 (Whittaker functions, and the Fourier coefficients as local Siegel series)
items.statement: Lemma 2.7: for a Hermitian O_{F′}-lattice L of rank n with fundamental matrix T and a generator θ of ω_{O_F}, W_{Tθ}(1, s, Φ) = L_{n,F′/F}(s)^{−1}Den(q^{−2s}, L), where L_{n,F′/F}(s) = Π_{i=1}^n L(i + 2s, η^i). Theorem 2.8: for a rank n vector bundle E on X′, E^{reg}(m(E), s, Φ) = Σ_{a : E ↪ σ^*E^∨}E_a(m(E), s, Φ) over injective Hermitian maps, and E_a(m(E), s, Φ) = χ(det E)q^{−deg(E)(s−n/2)−n²deg(ω_X)/2}L_n(s)^{−1}Den(q^{−2s}, (E, a)), where L_n(s) = Π_{i=1}^nL(i+2s, η^i) and Den(q^{−2s}, (E,a)) is the product of the local Siegel series of the Hermitian lattices at all places.
items.locator: Lemma 2.7 and Theorem 2.8, pp. 584–586, published version
items.note: Routed to FunctionFieldArithmetic FA.6 as a source. The paper proves Lemma 2.7 in the inert case and only asserts that the split case is "easily modified".

items.name: §3.1–3.2 (étale charts for Coh_d(X) and Laumon's Springer sheaf)
items.statement: Coh_d(X) is the moduli stack of torsion coherent sheaves of length d on a smooth curve X. Lemma 3.1 characterizes the divisors in U_d ∖ R_{d,f} for an étale chart (U, f) of X, and Lemma 3.2 shows that f^{Coh}_d : Coh_d(U) → Coh_d(A¹) is étale on Coh_d(U)_f and that these substacks cover Coh_d(X), so Coh_d(X) is étale locally [gl_d/GL_d]. Lemma 3.3 (Laumon): the flag stack C̃oh_d(X) and Coh_d(X) are smooth of dimension zero and the forgetful map π^{Coh}_{d,X} is proper and small; Corollary 3.4: Spr_d := Rπ^{Coh}_{d,X,*}Q_ℓ is a perverse sheaf, the middle extension of its restriction to the locus of multiplicity-free support, so the geometric S_d-action extends to all of Spr_d.
items.note: This globalizes the Springer sheaf of gl_d over the curve, following Laumon [15, Theorem 3.3.1]. Routed to the new Part II ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil (parent GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands).

items.name: §3.3–3.4 (Springer fibres over Coh_d(X), Lemmas 3.5–3.6, Corollary 3.7 and Proposition 3.8)
items.statement: For Q ∈ Coh_d(X)(k̄) with support divisor D and Z = (supp D)(k̄), the Springer fibre B_Q classifies complete flags of subsheaves and decomposes as ⊔_{y ∈ Σ(Z)}B_Q(y) over the maps y : {1, …, d} → Z with Σy(i) = D. Lemma 3.5: w ∈ S_d sends H^*(B_Q(y)) to H^*(B_Q(y ∘ w^{−1})); Lemma 3.6: for w of minimal length with y ∘ w^{−1} = y′ the Springer action is induced by the canonical isomorphism B_Q(y) ≅ B_Q(y′), hence sends fundamental class to fundamental class; Corollary 3.7: H^*(B_Q) ≅ Ind^{S_d}_{S_y}(⊗_{x ∈ Z}H^*(B_{Q_x})). Proposition 3.8: the stalk of the sign-isotypic summand St_d vanishes at non-semisimple Q, and at a semisimple Q = ⊕_v k_v^{⊕d_v} it is one-dimensional with Frobenius acting by ε(Q)Π_v q_v^{d_v(d_v−1)/2}.
items.locator: §§3.3–3.4, Lemmas 3.5–3.6, Corollary 3.7, Proposition 3.8, pp. 589–593, published version
items.note: Routed to the new Part II ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil (parent GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands).

items.name: §4.1 (the stack Herm_d(X′/X) of Hermitian torsion sheaves and its local model [o_d/O_d])
items.statement: Herm_d(X′/X) classifies torsion sheaves Q on X′ of length d with a Hermitian structure h : Q ≅ σ^*Q^∨ (Q^∨ = Ext¹(Q, ω_{X′})). Remark 4.1: for ν étale it is empty for odd d. Lemma 4.2: Herm_d(A¹_{√t}/A¹_t) ≅ [o_d/O_d], the quotient of the orthogonal Lie algebra. Lemma 4.3: σ-equivariant étale charts make Herm_d(X′/X) étale locally isomorphic to [o_d/O_d] when ν is ramified at at most one point, and in general Herm_d(X′/X) is smooth of dimension 0. Remark 4.4 records the skew-Hermitian analogue with [sp_d/Sp_d].
items.locator: §4.1, Remark 4.1, Lemmas 4.2–4.3, Remark 4.4, pp. 593–596, published version
items.note: Routed to the new Part II ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil (parent GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands).

items.name: §4.2–4.3 (the Hermitian Springer sheaf Spr^{Herm}_{2d}, its W_d-action and Definition 4.7)
items.statement: H̃erm_d(X′/X) classifies (Q, h) with a full isotropic flag 0 ⊂ Q_1 ⊂ ⋯ ⊂ Q_{d−1} = Q_1^⊥ ⊂ Q_d = Q. Proposition 4.5: π^{Herm}_d is étale locally the Grothendieck alteration [õ_d/O_d] → [o_d/O_d] (when ν is ramified at at most one point), and in general H̃erm_d is smooth of dimension 0 and π^{Herm}_d is small, so Spr^{Herm}_d := Rπ^{Herm}_{d,*}Q_ℓ is the middle extension of its restriction to the open locus. Corollary 4.6: for ν étale there is a canonical W_d = (Z/2Z)^d ⋊ S_d-action on Spr^{Herm}_{2d}. Definition 4.7: Spr^{Herm}_{2d}[ρ] := (ρ^∨ ⊗ Spr^{Herm}_{2d})^{W_d} for a representation ρ of W_d, and HSpr_d := (Spr^{Herm}_{2d})^{(Z/2Z)^d} with its S_d-action. Remark 4.8 gives the ramified variant indexed by parities at the ramification locus.
items.locator: §§4.2–4.3, Proposition 4.5, Corollary 4.6, Definition 4.7, Remark 4.8, pp. 596–597, published version
items.note: The Hermitian analogue of Laumon's construction: a global Springer sheaf for o_{2d} over Herm_{2d}(X′/X). Routed to the new Part II ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil (parent GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands).

items.name: §4.4–4.6 (Hermitian Springer fibres and the comparison with Coh_d: Lemmas 4.9–4.12, Propositions 4.11 and 4.13)
items.statement: Lemma 4.9: w ∈ W_d permutes the pieces H^*(B^{Herm}_Q(y′)) of the Hermitian Springer fibre; Lemma 4.10: a minimal-length w acts by the canonical isomorphism γ_{y′,y″}. Let Lagr_{2d} classify Lagrangian subsheaves L ⊂ Q; Proposition 4.11: there is a canonical S_d-equivariant isomorphism υ^{♦,*}_{2d}HSpr_d ≅ ε^{♦,*}_dSpr_d over the locus (X′_d)^♦ where the support divisor is disjoint from its conjugate. Lemma 4.12: there is a canonical bijection |Herm_{2d}(X′/X)(k)| ≅ |Coh_d(X)(k)| respecting supports, Q ↦ Q^♭. Proposition 4.13: under the induced isomorphism of stalks, Frob_Q corresponds to Frob_{Q^♭} ∘ θ, where θ is the involution that is ±1 on the ± parts of H^*(B_{Q^♭}).
items.locator: §§4.4–4.6, Lemmas 4.9–4.12, Propositions 4.11 and 4.13, pp. 597–606, published version
items.note: These comparisons are what convert the signs in the Cho–Yamauchi formula into the Frobenius traces of Hermitian Springer sheaves. Routed to the new Part II ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil (parent GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands).

items.name: §5 (geometrization of local densities: Theorem 5.1, Definition 5.2 and Theorem 5.3)
items.statement: Theorem 5.1 restates Theorem 2.8 with the local Siegel series of the cokernel: E_a(m(E), s, Φ) = χ(det E)q^{−deg(E)(s−n/2)−n²deg(ω_X)/2}L_n(s)^{−1}Den(q^{−2s}, coker(a)). Definition 5.2 introduces the graded virtual perverse sheaves on Herm_{2d}: P_d(T) = ⊕_{j=0}^d(−1)^j(HSpr_d)^{(S_j × S_{d−j}, sgn_j ⊠ 1)}T^j and K^{Eis}_d(T) = ⊕_{i=0}^d R(←f_i)_!R(→f_i)^*(Q_ℓ·T^i ⊠ P_{d−i}(T)), where Herm_{i,2d} classifies an isotropic subsheaf I ⊂ Q of length i. Theorem 5.3: Den(T, Q) = Tr(Fr, K^{Eis}_d(T)_Q) for every Q ∈ Herm_{2d}(k). Here the global Den(T, Q) of a Hermitian torsion sheaf Q is the product over places v of the local polynomials Den_v(T^{deg v}, Q_v) = Σ_{I ⊂ I^⊥ ⊂ Q_v}T^{2ℓ_v(I)}m_v(t′_v(I^⊥/I); T^{deg v}) (§5.1), and coker(a) carries the Hermitian structure induced by a (§5.1).
items.locator: §§5.1–5.2, Theorem 5.1, Definition 5.2, Theorem 5.3, pp. 606–608, published version
items.note: Routed to the new Part II ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil (parent GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands).

items.name: §5.3–5.5 (the factorized computation: Lemma 5.4, Propositions 5.5–5.7)
items.statement: Lemma 5.4 and Proposition 5.5 factor the graded traces P_Q(T) over the places of the support, with P_{Q_v}(T) = P_{Q^♭_v}(T) at split v and the twisted form at inert v; Proposition 5.6: for Q^♭ ∈ Coh_d(X)(k), P_{Q^♭}(T) = Π_{v ∈ |Z|}Π_{j=0}^{t_v(Q^♭)−1}(1 − q_v^jT^{deg v}); Proposition 5.7: for Q ∈ Herm_{2d}(X′/X)(k), P_Q(T) = Π_v m_v(t′_v(Q); T^{deg v}) = Π_{v ∈ |Z|}Π_{j=0}^{t′_v(Q)−1}(1 − (η(ϖ_v)q_v)^jT^{deg v}), which is exactly the weight factor of the Cho–Yamauchi formula.
items.note: Routed to the new Part II ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil (parent GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands).

items.name: §6.1 (Hermitian bundles and Bun_{U(n)})
items.statement: A rank n Hermitian (unitary) bundle on X × S is a rank n bundle F on X′ × S with h : F ≅ σ^*F^∨ satisfying σ^*h^∨ = h; Bun_{U(n)} is their moduli stack. Remark 6.2: this groupoid is equivalent to that of torsors for the group scheme U(n) = {g ∈ Res_{X′/X}GL_n : σ(^tg^{−1}) = g} over X, using a square root ω^{1/2}_X and the standard Hermitian bundle (F_n, h_n) = (ν^*ω^{1/2}_X, h_1)^{⊕n} (the paper prints ν^*ω^{1/2}_{X′}, E15). Throughout, ∨ is the ω_{X′}-twisted dual Hom(−, ω_{X′}); this is what makes F_1 self-dual and gives d = −χ(X′, E). dim Bun_{U(n)} = n²(g − 1), used but not stated in the paper.
items.note: GS.0 plans Bun_G on the global curve for a smooth (possibly nonsplit) group scheme with level structures and descent data; U(n) is such a group scheme.

items.name: §6.2–6.3 (Hecke stacks and the moduli of Hermitian shtukas Sht^r_{U(n)})
items.statement: Hk^r_{U(n)} classifies legs x′_i ∈ X′(S), Hermitian bundles (F_i, h_i) and modifications f_i : F_{i−1} ⇢ F_i that are lower of length 1 at x′_i and upper of length 1 at σ(x′_i) (Definitions 6.3(3), 6.6(3)), compatibly with the Hermitian structures (Definitions 6.3–6.5); Sht^r_{U(n)} is the fibre product of Hk^r_{U(n)} with the graph of Frobenius, i.e. the moduli of chains F_0 ⇢ ⋯ ⇢ F_r ≅ ^τF_0 (Definition 6.6). Lemma 6.7: Sht^r_{U(n)} is empty if and only if r is odd (via the Prym variety and Wirtinger's result). Lemma 6.8: Bun_{U(n)} is smooth and equidimensional. Lemma 6.9: (pr_X, pr_r) : Hk^r_{U(n)} → (X′)^r × Bun_{U(n)} is smooth of relative dimension r(n−1), and Sht^r_{U(n)} is a Deligne–Mumford stack, locally of finite type, smooth separated and equidimensional of relative dimension r(n−1) over (X′)^r.
items.locator: §§6.2–6.4, Definitions 6.3–6.6, Lemma 6.7, Lemmas 6.8–6.9 (§6.4), pp. 614–617, published version
items.note: GS.1 plans global Hecke stacks and GS.2 multi-leg shtuka stacks with bounds and truncations for a general G; the unitary case with its Hermitian modifications is an instance. The U(n)-specific Lemmas 6.7 and 6.9 are item 34.

items.name: §7.1–7.4 (the special cycles Z^r_E and Z^r_E(a), and their finiteness)
items.statement: For a rank m bundle E on X′, Z^r_E classifies a U(n)-shtuka together with maps t_i : E ⊠ O_S → F_i compatible with the modifications and with ϕ : F_r ≅ ^τF_0 (Definition 7.1); the induced Hermitian maps E → σ^*E^∨ are independent of i and define a map Z^r_E → A^{all}_E(k) to the discrete set of Hermitian maps, whose fibre over a is Z^r_E(a) (Definition 7.2). D_a is the divisor on X with ν^{−1}(D_a) = div(det a) (Definition 7.3), and Z^r_E(a)° ⊆ Z^r_E(a) is the open locus where all t_i are fibrewise injective (Definition 7.4). Proposition 7.5: Z^r_E(a) → Sht^r_{U(n)} and Z^r_E(a)^* → Sht^r_{U(n)} are finite (using Lemma 7.6 on fixed points of an injective Frobenius-semilinear map). Lemma 7.7: for E = E_1 ⊕ E_2 the fibre product of Z^r_{E_1}(a_1) and Z^r_{E_2}(a_2) over Sht^r_{U(n)} is the disjoint union of the Z^r_E(a) with the given diagonal blocks; Lemma 7.8: for s : E′ → E, the induced z_s : Z^r_E(a) → Z^r_{E′}(a′) is a closed embedding if s is generically surjective, and open and closed over (X ∖ ν(D_s))^r if s is generically an isomorphism.
items.locator: §§7.1–7.4, Definitions 7.1–7.4, Proposition 7.5, Lemmas 7.6–7.8, pp. 617–622, published version
items.note: These are the function-field analogues of the Kudla–Rapoport cycles; for E a line bundle they are the analogues of Kudla–Rapoport divisors, of codimension at least r (Proposition 7.9; equality for a ≠ 0 is only announced, Remark 7.10). Routed to the new Part II ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil (parent GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands).

items.name: §7.5 and §9 (corank one cycles have the expected dimension: Proposition 7.9, Definition 7.11, Propositions 9.1 and 9.5)
items.statement: Proposition 7.9: dim Z^r_L(a)° ≤ r(n−1) for a line bundle L; this is proved in §9 by stratifying Z = Z^r_L(a)° according to the zero divisors D_i of the maps t_i (Proposition 9.1 for a ≠ 0 and n ≥ 2: the geometric fibres of π[D_•] : Z[D_•] → (X′_{k̄})^{I_0} have dimension ≤ (n−1)|I_+| + (n−2)|I_0|, each stratum has dimension ≤ (n−1)(|I_+| + |I_0|) ≤ r(n−1), with the equality case described; Claim 9.2 gives the smoothness of Π[D_•]; n = 1 is treated separately) and, for a = 0, by the strata Z[N; I_•] with |I_+| = |I_−| (a cover, not a partition as printed, E21) (Proposition 9.5, using the quasi-finiteness Lemma 9.4 and the semilinear-fibre Lemma 9.3, a variant of [14, Lemma 2.13]). Definition 7.11: [Z^r_L(a)°] ∈ Ch_{r(n−1)}(Z^r_L(a)°) is the cycle class of the union of the irreducible components of dimension exactly r(n−1). Remark 7.10 announces that for a ≠ 0 the stack Z^r_L(a)° is in fact LCI of pure dimension r(n−1).
items.locator: §7.5, Proposition 7.9, Definition 7.11, Remark 7.10, pp. 623; §9, Propositions 9.1, 9.5, Claim 9.2, Lemmas 9.3–9.4, pp. 634–640, published version
items.note: Routed to the new Part II ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil (parent GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands).

items.name: §7.6–7.9 (corank n cycles: Lemma 7.12, Proposition 7.13, good framings and the class ζ^r_{L_1,…,L_n}(a))
items.statement: For E of rank n and a ∈ A_E(k): Lemma 7.12 shows the legs of a point of Z^r_E(a) lie in supp ν^{−1}(D_a); Proposition 7.13: Z^r_E(a) is a proper scheme over k depending only on the Hermitian torsion sheaf Q = coker(a) = σ^*E^∨/E (proved in §8.4.1). When E = ⊕L_i, the intersection of the classes [Z^r_{L_i}(a_{ii})] over Sht^r_{U(n)} defines ζ^r_{L_1,…,L_n}(a) ∈ Ch_0(Z^r_E(a)) (§7.8). Definition 7.15: a good framing of (E, a) is an injective s = ⊕s_i : E′ = ⊕_{i=1}^nL_i → E with ν(D_s) disjoint from D_a; Lemma 7.16: good framings exist; Corollary 7.17: a good framing realizes Z^r_E(a) as an open and closed subscheme of Z^r_{E′}(a′), so that Definition-Proposition 7.18 sets [Z^r_E(a)] := ζ^r_{L_1,…,L_n}(a′)|_{Z^r_E(a)} ∈ Ch_0(Z^r_E(a)) — its independence of the good framing is Theorem 10.1, and Z^r_E(a) is proper, so deg[Z^r_E(a)] ∈ Q is defined.
items.locator: §§7.6–7.9, Lemma 7.12, Proposition 7.13, Remark 7.14, Definition 7.15, Lemma 7.16, Corollary 7.17, Definition-Proposition 7.18, pp. 623–626, published version
items.note: Routed to the new Part II ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil (parent GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands). ζ is the product of the classes [Z^r_{L_i}(a_ii)°] of Definition 7.11, restricted to the open and closed Z^r_E(a) ⊂ Z^r_{L_1,…,L_n}(a_11,…,a_nn)°.

items.name: §8.1–8.3 (Hitchin-type moduli stacks M(m, n), the Hitchin base A(m) and Hitchin shtukas)
items.statement: M^{all}(m, n) classifies (E, (F, h), t : E → F) with E of rank m, (F, h) a rank n Hermitian bundle, and M(m,n) is the open substack where t is fibrewise injective (Definition 8.1); A^{all}(m) classifies (E, a : E → σ^*E^∨) with σ(a^∨) = a, and A(m) the injective locus (Definition 8.2); the Hitchin fibration f : M^{all} → A^{all} sends (E, (F,h), t) to a = σ^*t^∨ ∘ h ∘ t (Definition 8.3), and sends M(n,n) into A(n) (Remark 8.4). Definition 8.5 gives the Hecke stacks Hk^r_M and Definition 8.6 the Hitchin shtukas Sht^r_M as the fibre product of Hk^r_M with the graph of Frobenius; (8.3) exhibits Z^r_E(a)° as the fibre of Sht^r_M → A(k) over (E, a) (and Z^r_E(a) as that of Sht^r_{M^{all}}), up to the finite étale quotient by Aut(a)(k). Definition 8.3 assumes 1 ≤ m ≤ n.
items.note: The Hitchin-type stack is what appears when the intersections defining the special cycle are performed in a different order, with the Frobenius intersection left to the end. Routed to the new Part II ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil (parent GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands).

items.name: §8.4–8.5 (from bundles to torsion sheaves: Lemmas 8.8, 8.10, 8.11, Proposition 8.12, Corollaries 8.9 and 8.13)
items.statement: For m = n and d = −χ(X′, E), M_d and A_d are the corresponding open-closed substacks, and Lemma 8.8 gives a Cartesian square relating f_d : M_d → A_d to υ_{2d} : Lagr_{2d} → Herm_{2d} (a subsheaf L ⊂ σ^*E^∨/E is Lagrangian iff the corresponding E ⊂ F ⊂ σ^*E^∨ is self-dual). Corollary 8.9: f_d is proper. Lemma 8.10: υ_{2d} is small. Lemma 8.11: β_d : M_d → Coh_d(X′) × Bun_{U(n)} is smooth of relative dimension dn, so M_d is smooth of pure dimension dn + n²(g−1). Proposition 8.12: g : A_d → Herm_{2d} is smooth. Corollary 8.13: the Hitchin fibration f : M_d → A_d is small, so Rf_*Q_ℓ is a shifted perverse sheaf, the middle extension from any dense open.
items.locator: §§8.4–8.5, Lemmas 8.8, 8.10–8.11, Proposition 8.12, Corollaries 8.9 and 8.13, pp. 629–632, published version
items.note: Routed to the new Part II ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil (parent GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands).

items.name: §8.6 (the 0-cycle class [Sht^r_{M_d}] from Hitchin shtukas)
items.statement: Lemma 8.14: Hk^1_{M_d} is smooth and equidimensional of the same dimension as M_d (via almost Hermitian bundles with defect at a conjugate pair). Definition 8.15 introduces Φ^r_S : S^{r+1} → S^{2r+2}, ξ ↦ (ξ_0, ξ_1, ξ_1, …, ξ_r, ξ_r, Fr(ξ_0)), realizing Sht^r_{M_d} as a fibre product; Definition 8.16 defines [Sht^r_{M_d}] ∈ Ch_0(Sht^r_{M_d}) as the refined Gysin pullback (Φ^r_{M_d})^![(Hk^1_{M_d})^r × M_d], which makes sense because M_d is smooth and equidimensional.
items.note: Routed to the new Part II ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil (parent GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands).

items.name: Theorems 10.1–10.2 and Lemma 10.3 (independence of the good framing)
items.statement: Theorem 10.1: for E of rank n, a ∈ A_E(k) and any good framing s : E′ = ⊕L_i ↪ E with induced a′, ζ^r_{L_1,…,L_n}(a′)|_{Z^r_E(a)} = [Sht^r_{M(n,n)}]|_{Z^r_E(a)} in Ch_0(Z^r_E(a)); in particular the left-hand side is independent of the framing, so the class [Z^r_E(a)] of Definition-Proposition 7.18, defined through a good framing, is independent of the framing and equals [Sht^r_{M(n,n)}]|_{Z^r_E(a)}. Theorem 10.2 is the same statement for very good framings when X′ is geometrically connected (the paper says "connected", E28), and Lemma 10.3 deduces Theorem 10.1 from it by twisting the L_i down by divisors.
items.note: Routed to the new Part II ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil (parent GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands).

items.name: §10.2–10.4 (auxiliary Hitchin stacks, the étale maps of Lemmas 10.5–10.6 and the comparisons 10.7–10.8)
items.statement: Lemma 10.4: the auxiliary stacks M_d (line bundles L_i with χ = −d_i, the slope condition (10.3) and maps t′_i with ⊕t′_i injective) and Hk^1_{M_d} are smooth of pure dimension dn − (n²−2n)(g−1). Lemma 10.5: the maps w_1 and h_1 relating the auxiliary Hitchin stacks are étale (the paper also claims u_1 is étale, which fails in general; E22); Lemma 10.6: u_1 (resp. u_2) restricted to each connected component of Sht^r_{M_{d,e}} is an isomorphism onto a component of Sht^r_{M_d} (resp. Sht^r_{M_e}). Lemmas 10.7–10.8: u_1^*[Sht^r_{M_d}] = [Sht^r_{M_{d,e}}] = u_2^*[Sht^r_{M_e}].
items.note: Routed to the new Part II ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil (parent GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands).

items.name: Proposition 10.9 and Lemma 10.10 (compatibility of refined Gysin maps, and the framing comparison)
items.statement: Proposition 10.9: for a smooth representable base change u : A′ → A the refined Gysin classes match, u^*_{Sht}Φ^!_M(ζ × [M]) = Φ^!_{M′}u^*_H(ζ × [M]). Lemma 10.10: for E′ = ⊕L_i and a′ ∈ A_d(k), [Sht^r_{M_d}]|_{Z^r_{E′}(a′)^♡} = ζ^r_{L_1,…,L_n}(a′) on the open part Z^♡ where the slope condition holds (as printed it is stated on all of Z^r_{E′}(a′), E28), proved by applying the Octahedron Lemma of [28, Theorem A.10] to a diagram of rigidified moduli stacks and exchanging the order of the linear and Frobenius intersections. §10.5 treats the geometrically disconnected cases X′ = X ⊔ X and X′ = X_{k′}.
items.note: Routed to the new Part II ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil (parent GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands).

items.name: §11.1 (the Hecke correspondence on Lagr_{2d}: Lemma 11.1, Proposition 11.2, Corollary 11.3)
items.statement: Lemma 11.1: Hk^1_{Lagr_{2d}}, the moduli of (0 ⊂ L′ ⊂ L ⊂ Q, h) with L Lagrangian and L/L′ of length one, is smooth of dimension zero (locally [p/P] for a parabolic in O_{2d}). Proposition 11.2: [Sht^r_{M_d}] = g^*_{Sht}[Sht^r_{Lagr_{2d}}] in Ch_0(Sht^r_{M_d}), by Proposition 10.9 applied to the smooth map g : A_d → Herm_{2d}. Corollary 11.3: for (E, a) ∈ A_d(k) with Q = coker(a), [Z^r_E(a)] corresponds to [Z^r_Q]; in particular deg[Z^r_E(a)] = deg[Z^r_Q] depends only on the Hermitian torsion sheaf. Hk^r_{Lagr_{2d}} and Sht^r_{Lagr_{2d}} are defined in (11.1)–(11.2), [Sht^r_{Lagr_{2d}}] := Φ^!_{Lagr_{2d}}[(Hk^1_{Lagr_{2d}})^r × Lagr_{2d}], and [Z^r_Q] := [Sht^r_{Lagr_{2d}}]|_{Z^r_Q}, with Z^r_Q the fibre over Spec k → Herm_{2d}(k) at Q.
items.locator: §11.1, Lemma 11.1, Proposition 11.2, Corollary 11.3, pp. 654–655, published version
items.note: Routed to the new Part II ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil (parent GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands).

items.name: §11.2 (the sheaf K^{Int}_d: Lemma 11.4, Corollary 11.5, Definition 11.6 and Proposition 11.7)
items.statement: Lemma 11.4: R(υ_{2d})_*Q_ℓ ≅ (Spr^{Herm}_{2d})^{S_d}. With Ind^{W_d}_{S_d}1 = ⊕_{i=0}^dρ_i, where ρ_i = Ind^{W_d}_{(Z/2)^d ⋊ (S_i × S_{d−i})}(χ_i ⊠ 1) and χ_i is nontrivial exactly on the first i factors of (Z/2)^d, Corollary 11.5 gives R(υ_{2d})_*Q_ℓ ≅ ⊕_{i=0}^dSpr^{Herm}_{2d}[ρ_i], and Definition 11.6 sets K^{Int}_d(T) := ⊕_{i=0}^dSpr^{Herm}_{2d}[ρ_i]T^i. Proposition 11.7: the cohomological correspondence (υ_{2d})_![Hk^1_{Lagr_{2d}}] preserves this decomposition and acts on Spr^{Herm}_{2d}[ρ_i] by the scalar (d − 2i).
items.locator: §11.2, Lemma 11.4, Corollary 11.5, Definition 11.6, Proposition 11.7, pp. 655–657, published version
items.note: Routed to the new Part II ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil (parent GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands).

items.name: §11.3–11.4 (the Lefschetz trace formula for Hitchin shtukas: Proposition 11.8 and Corollaries 11.9–11.10)
items.statement: Proposition 11.8: for a self-correspondence built from cohomological correspondences ζ_i, deg((Φ^!_M(ζ_1 × ⋯ × ζ_r × [M]))|_{Sht_C|_s}) = Tr(f_!cl(ζ_1) ∘ ⋯ ∘ f_!cl(ζ_r) ∘ Fr_s, (Rf_!Q_ℓ)_s), first for schemes of finite type and then in general. Corollary 11.9: deg[Z^r_Q] = Tr([Hk^1_{Lagr_{2d}}]^r ∘ Fr, (R(υ_{2d})_*Q_ℓ)_Q) = Σ_{i=0}^d(d − 2i)^rTr(Fr, Spr^{Herm}_{2d}[ρ_i]_Q). Corollary 11.10: deg[Z^r_E(a)] = (1/(log q)^r)(d/ds)^r|_{s=0}(q^{ds}Tr(Fr, K^{Int}_d(q^{−2s})_Q)).
items.note: Routed to the new Part II ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil (parent GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands).

items.name: Lemmas 11.11–11.13 and Corollary 11.14 (the geometric functional equation and the vanishing for odd r)
items.statement: Lemma 11.11: Spr^{Herm}_{2d}[ρ_d] ≅ η^{Herm}_{2d}, the rank one local system pulled back from the quadratic character; Lemma 11.12: T^dK^{Int}_d(T^{−1}) ≅ η^{Herm}_{2d} ⊗ K^{Int}_d(T), i.e. Spr^{Herm}_{2d}[ρ_{d−i}] ≅ η^{Herm}_{2d} ⊗ Spr^{Herm}_{2d}[ρ_i]; Lemma 11.13: Tr(Fr, η^{Herm}_{2d}|_Q) = 1 whenever Q comes from some (E, a) ∈ A_d(k), by the triviality of η_{F′/F} on norms. Corollary 11.14: s ↦ q^{ds}Tr(Fr, K^{Int}_d(q^{−2s})_Q) is even, so all odd derivatives vanish at s = 0 — consistent with Sht^r_{U(n)} = ∅ for odd r.
items.note: Routed to the new Part II ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil (parent GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands).

items.name: §12 (Theorems 12.1–12.2, Proposition 12.3 and Lemma 12.4: the matching of the two sheaves)
items.statement: Theorem 12.2 (from Theorems 2.8 and 5.3): Ẽ_a(m(E), s, Φ) = Tr(Fr, K^{Eis}_d(q^{−2s})_Q). With Corollary 11.10 this reduces Theorem 12.1 (= Theorem 1.1) to Proposition 12.3: K^{Int}_d(T) ≅ K^{Eis}_d(T) as graded perverse sheaves on Herm_{2d}(X′/X). Writing both as Spr^{Herm}_{2d}[ρ] for graded virtual W_d-representations, the proposition becomes an identity of virtual representations, proved through Lemma 12.4: χ_d = Σ_{j=0}^d(−1)^jInd^{W_d}_{S_{d−j} × W_j}(1 ⊠ sgn̄_j), where sgn̄_j is the sign of S_j inflated to W_j (not the Coxeter sign of W_j), verified by comparing traces of an arbitrary g ∈ W_d.
items.locator: §12, Theorems 12.1–12.2, Proposition 12.3, Lemma 12.4, pp. 661–666, published version
items.note: Routed to the new Part II ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil (parent GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands). The reduction in Proposition 12.3 rests on the Springer-theory translation of K^{Eis} (Theorem 5.3 and §5.3) and a parabolic-induction step asserted without proof. The review checked Lemma 12.4, (11.5) and the graded identity for d ≤ 6.

items.name: Perverse sheaves, small maps, middle extension and the decomposition theorem
items.statement: The middle perverse t-structure, intermediate extensions and the fact that the direct image of the constant sheaf along a small map is the middle extension of its restriction to the open locus where the map is finite étale; the decomposition theorem for proper maps; used for Spr_d, Spr^{Herm}_{2d}, R(υ_{2d})_*Q_ℓ and Rf_*Q_ℓ.
items.note: EDC.5 plans the perverse t-structure and intermediate extension, EDC.7 purity and the decomposition theorem.

items.name: Cohomological correspondences, the Grothendieck–Lefschetz trace formula and the sheaf-to-function dictionary
items.statement: Cohomological correspondences c_2^*K → c_1^!K with their composition and trace, and the Grothendieck–Lefschetz trace formula computing Frobenius traces of direct images; the sheaf-to-function dictionary used to pass between perverse sheaves on Herm_{2d}(X′/X) and functions on its k-points.
items.note: EDC.8 plans cohomological correspondences and their trace classes; R34.1 the Frobenius/weight conventions. Proposition 11.8 rests on the Lefschetz trace formula of [YZ17, Proposition A.12] (routed to EDC.8 by PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-17).

items.name: Chow groups of stacks, refined Gysin maps and intersection products
items.statement: The rationalized Chow groups of the algebraic stacks in play, proper pushforward, refined Gysin pullback along a regular embedding (used for Φ^!_{M_d} in Definition 8.16 and in Proposition 10.9), intersection products of cycle classes, and the Octahedron Lemma of [28, Theorem A.10] for exchanging the order of two refined intersections.
items.note: SF.5 plans Chow groups, refined Gysin maps and intersection products; the Octahedron Lemma of Yun–Zhang is an addition made in the Part II brief.

items.name: §12.3 (the split case X′ = X ⊔ X made explicit)
items.statement: For X′ = X ⊔ X one has H_n = GL_{2n,F} with P_n the (n,n) parabolic and I_n(s) = Ind(|·|^{s+n/2}_F × |·|^{−s−n/2}_F); for E = (E_1, E_2) and an injective a : E_1 → E^∨_2, E_a(m(E), s, Φ) = q^{−(deg E_1 + deg E_2)(s−n/2) − n²deg ω_X/2}L_n(s)^{−1}Den(q^{−2s}, E^∨_2/E_1) with L_n(s) = Π_{i=1}^nζ_F(i+2s) and Den(T, Q) = Σ_{0 ⊂ I_1 ⊂ I_2 ⊂ Q}T^{dim I_1 + dim Q/I_2}Π_v m_v(t_v(I_2/I_1); T^{deg v}), so Ẽ_a = Den(q^{−2s}, E^∨_2/E_1). Geometrically (X′)^r = ⊔_{μ ∈ {±1}^r}X^r, Sht^r_{U(n)} = ⊔_μ Sht^μ_{U(n)} with Sht^μ_{U(n)} ≅ Sht^μ_{GL_n} (the Yun–Zhang moduli of GL_n-shtukas with upper/lower modifications prescribed by μ, empty unless Σμ_i = 0), and Z^r_E = ⊔_μ Z^μ_E with Z^μ_E(a) proper carrying a class [Z^μ_E(a)]; the main theorem becomes Σ_{μ ∈ {±1}^r}deg[Z^μ_E(a)] = (1/(log q)^r)(d/ds)^r|_{s=0}(q^{ds}Ẽ_a(m(E), s, Φ)) with d = −(χ(X, E_1) + χ(X, E_2)); the individual deg[Z^μ_E(a)] are not independent of μ.
items.note: Routed to the new Part II ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil (parent GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands). The formula for E_a is for χ = 1; for a general unramified χ an extra factor χ(det E) appears in E_a, but Ẽ_a is unchanged.

items.name: Lemmas 6.7 and 6.9 for U(n): emptiness for odd r and the P^{n−1}-bundle structure of Hk^1_{U(n)}
items.statement: Lemma 6.7: Sht^r_{U(n)} is empty if and only if r is odd. For n = 1, Sht^r_{U(1)} is the fibre product of the Lang map Bun_{U(1)} → Prym(X′/X), F ↦ F^{−1} ⊗ ^τF, with (X′)^r → Prym(X′/X), D ↦ O(σD − D). For geometrically connected X′, Wirtinger's result makes the parity decide which of the two components is hit. For X ⊔ X the Lang map lands in the identity component, and for X_{k′} in the components indexed by 2Z. General n reduces to n = 1 by the determinant and direct sums. Lemma 6.9: (pr_X, pr_r) : Hk^r_{U(n)} → (X′)^r × Bun_{U(n)} is smooth of relative dimension r(n − 1), through the r-fold composition of Hk^1_{U(n)}, whose fibres are P^{n−1}-bundles (a hyperplane in F_{1,σ(x′)}); hence dim Sht^r_{U(n)} = rn.
items.note: Split off by the review from item 15. These U(n)-specific statements are the dimension input for §§7.7–7.8 and Lemma 8.14, and GS.2 plans only general smoothness. The printed proof of Lemma 6.7 is wrong in the X_{k′} case and has a sign slip in the square (E13, E14).

routes.title: Global shtukas and Langlands over function fields, Part II: special cycles on shtuka moduli and the higher Siegel–Weil formula
routes.reason: The objects are cycles on the moduli of G-shtukas and a Hitchin-type moduli stack over a curve, and the theorem is an identity between their degrees and the Taylor coefficients of an Eisenstein series: this is the direction of GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands, which owns Bun_G, Hecke and shtuka stacks and their cohomology but plans no special cycles, no Hitchin fibration and no arithmetic Siegel–Weil formula. It is not GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights work: nothing here is a height pairing, the intersections are 0-cycle degrees on function-field moduli, and the parallel unitary Part IIs there (UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles, UnitaryArithmeticInnerProductFormula) are about integral models of Shimura varieties. The Hermitian Springer theory of §§3–5 is planned here rather than in EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.2b, which owns Ngô's Hitchin fibration and affine Springer fibres for reductive groups: this is a different construction (global Springer sheaves on moduli of torsion sheaves) built for this proof.

GN.3 constructs local representation densities and mass formulas. This source adds the Hermitian case in the form needed for Siegel series: the density Den(M, L) of integral representations of Hermitian O_{F′}-lattices with dim(Rep_{M,L})_F = n(2m−n), including the split algebra F′ = F × F where a Hermitian lattice is a pair with a perfect pairing; the weight polynomials m(a; T) = Π_{i=0}^{a−1}(1 − (η(ϖ)q)^iT); and the Cho–Yamauchi formula (Theorem 2.3) in both the inert and the split case, with the resulting normalized local Siegel series Den(T, L), its dependence only on the Hermitian torsion module L^∨/L, and its functional equation. PAPER-LI-ZHANG-22-B and PAPER-LI-LIU-22 route the same family of local densities to GN.3.

FA.6 constructs automorphic forms for a reductive group over a function field, with cuspidal spaces, Hecke correspondences and the unramified Satake dictionary. This source adds the Siegel–Eisenstein series of the quasi-split unitary group U(W) for a split skew-Hermitian space of dimension 2n over a function field: the degenerate principal series with its everywhere unramified section (Remark 2.1 shows the character χ can be chosen unramified, using the alternating cup product on H^1(X, Z/2)), the Fourier expansion along the Siegel unipotent radical against the residue pairing, the factorization of non-singular coefficients into local Whittaker functions with the measure factor |ω_X|^{−n²/2}, the identification of the local Whittaker function with the local Siegel series (Lemma 2.7) and the resulting formula for the coefficients indexed by Hermitian maps a : E → σ^*E^∨ (Theorem 2.8).
